_source: ESC 2021 CVD Prevention · AHA 2024 Resistance Training Statement · ACSM FITT 2024 · ADA 2024 · NICE NG238 · WHO 2023
_patient_profile: Urban Sri Lankan upper-middle-class. Western-influenced diet. Gym access. English-literate. Familiar with Mediterranean concepts.

diet.recommended_pattern: Mediterranean diet adapted for urban Sri Lankan upper-middle-class
diet.evidence: 48% reduction in MACE (OR 0.52); 23% reduced all-cause mortality (Hareer 2025, 87 studies, >1.4M participants); ESC 2021 Class I Level A

foods_to_reduce.coconut_oil: High in saturated fat — switch to extra-virgin olive oil for cooking
foods_to_reduce.white_rice: GI 72–83; replace one meal/day with brown rice (GI 48–55), quinoa (35–53), or barley
foods_to_reduce.refined_carbohydrates: Raise TG and lower HDL — white bread, pasta, pastries
foods_to_reduce.saturated_fat_sources: Red meat fat, full-fat dairy, coconut milk curries (limit to 2×/week)
foods_to_reduce.salt_sources: Processed foods, instant noodles (Maggi), papadams, soy sauce, fish sauce
foods_to_reduce.fructose_rich: Soft drinks, fruit juices — NAFLD and TG risk

condition_specific.dyslipidaemia: Prioritise: oat beta-glucan 3g/day + plant sterols 2g/day + oily fish 2×/week + nuts 30g/day. Replace coconut oil with EVOO. Reduce saturated fat to <7%.
condition_specific.hypertension: DASH diet. Target <5g salt/day. Increase potassium (banana 420mg, avocado 485mg, sweet potato 540mg). Remove salt shaker from table.
condition_specific.diabetes_t2dm: Mediterranean + plate method (½ vegetables + ¼ lean protein + ¼ complex carbs). Post-meal 10–15 min walk reduces postprandial glucose 22% (Buffey 2022).
condition_specific.prediabetes: Low-GI carbohydrates. Plate method. Reduce white rice portion to ¾ cup cooked. Increase legumes.
condition_specific.nafld: Weight loss ≥7%. Restrict fructose and alcohol (complete). Mediterranean diet. 2+ cups coffee/day — 40% reduced liver fibrosis.
condition_specific.ckd: Protein 0.8g/kg/day. Salt <5g/day. Potassium restriction only if eGFR <30 (limit banana, avocado, chocolate). Phosphorus: limit dairy to 1 cup/day; avoid cola.
condition_specific.iron_deficiency: Haem iron 2–3×/week (lean red meat, liver, fish). Vitamin C with every iron-rich meal (lemon juice on lentils, orange juice). Delay tea/coffee 1 hour after meals — tannins reduce absorption 60%.
condition_specific.metabolic_syndrome: 500–750 kcal/day deficit. Largest meal at lunch. Avoid eating after 9pm. No meal skipping.

optimal_aerobic.note: Linear dose-response for CV outcomes above 150 min

resistance.note: Non-consecutive days; all major muscle groups; AHA 2024

intensity_guides.moderate: Talk but not sing; HR 50–70% max; RPE 12–14/20
intensity_guides.vigorous: Cannot maintain conversation; HR 70–85% max; RPE 15–17/20

condition_specific.dyslipidaemia: ≥200 min/week moderate-to-vigorous. Combined aerobic + resistance superior for lipid improvement (ESSA 2025). TG reduced -5.3 mg/dL, HDL +2.3 mg/dL.
condition_specific.hypertension: Daily aerobic preferred (BP lowering lasts 24h post-session). SBP reduction -4.9 to -12 mmHg with 150 min/week. Dynamic resistance only — avoid isometric holds and Valsalva.
condition_specific.diabetes_t2dm: Never 2 consecutive days without exercise (ADA rule). Post-meal 10–15 min walks — highest evidence for postprandial glucose. Check glucose before exercise if on insulin/sulphonylurea.
condition_specific.metabolic_syndrome: ≥250–300 min/week for weight reduction. Progressive 4-week ramp-up plan.
condition_specific.nafld: 150–200 min/week aerobic reduces hepatic fat 30–40% independently of weight loss.
condition_specific.post_mi: MANDATORY cardiac rehabilitation before any exercise prescription. Do not independently prescribe vigorous exercise.
condition_specific.ckd_g3: 150 min/week low-to-moderate intensity. Low-impact (walking, swimming, cycling). Medical clearance required if eGFR <45.

sample_week_general.sat: 45 min outdoor walk, cycling, tennis, or sport

accessibility_sri_lanka.gym: Full gym facilities common — treadmill, elliptical, free weights, cable machines, group classes
accessibility_sri_lanka.sport: Swimming (hotel/club pools, SSC, NCC, CCC), tennis, badminton, squash, golf (2 rounds ≈ 150 min)
accessibility_sri_lanka.home: Treadmill/exercise bike common. Peloton app, Nike Training Club, YouTube. Apple Watch / Garmin for tracking.
accessibility_sri_lanka.travel: Hotel gym. Bodyweight: squats, push-ups, lunges, plank.

osa_screen.action: Sleep study referral. CPAP reduces SBP 2–5 mmHg and improves glucose metabolism.

hygiene.environment: Dark, cool room 16–19°C. White noise app for urban noise.
hygiene.behaviour: Consistent bedtime 7 days/week. No screens 45–60 min before bed. No large meals within 2–3 hours. Limit caffeine after 2pm.
hygiene.relaxation: Mindfulness apps (Calm, Headspace). 4-7-8 breathing. Light evening yoga/stretching.

condition_specific.metabolic_syndrome_diabetes: Short sleep worsens insulin resistance and elevates cortisol. OSA screen essential.
condition_specific.hypertension: Each 1-hour sleep deficit raises SBP ~0.9 mmHg. OSA screen and CPAP as above.
condition_specific.dyslipidaemia: Short sleep associated with higher LDL and lower HDL. Target consistent 7–9 hours.

alcohol.position: WHO 2023: No safe level of alcohol. ESC 2021: As low as possible. NICE NG238: Reduce alcohol to reduce CVD risk.

risk_stratified.established_cvd_hf: Complete abstinence — directly cardiotoxic; AF trigger
risk_stratified.liver_disease: Complete abstinence — essential for hepatic recovery (NICE NG49)
risk_stratified.diabetes: Strongly counsel abstinence or major reduction — bidirectional glycaemic effects
risk_stratified.hypertension: Significant reduction — each unit raises SBP ~1–2 mmHg
risk_stratified.high_tg: Abstinence until normalised — alcohol acutely elevates TG
risk_stratified.high_cvd_risk_10pct: Minimal or abstinence — dose-response with CV events
risk_stratified.low_risk: Informed choice; WHO position discussed; if drinking: <14 units/week (M) / <7 (F); ≥2 alcohol-free days/week

counselling_points: Two drinks at dinner + two at the bar = 6–8 units in one evening
Alcohol-free alternatives: Heineken 0.0, sparkling water with citrus, mocktails
Red wine polyphenol benefit is small and outweighed by alcohol harms at >1 unit/day (ESC 2021)

lipids_new_statin_primary.reason: Check ≥40% non-HDL reduction; LFT safety; tolerance (NICE NG238)

bp_new_antihypertensive.reason: BP response; K+ and creatinine safety

new_t2dm.test: HbA1c + eGFR + uACR + lipids + eye + foot

sglt2i_started.reason: eGFR dip expected (acceptable ≤30%); DKA sick-day rules

ida_oral_iron.reason: Hb response ~10g/L rise per 2 weeks (NICE NG24)

cardiovascular: Central chest pain, pressure, or tightness — especially radiating to jaw, left arm, or back → A&E; call 1990
Sudden severe headache ('worst ever') — hypertensive crisis / SAH → A&E immediately
Sudden one-sided weakness, facial droop, or speech difficulty → stroke (FAST test) → A&E; call 1990
Sudden vision loss in one or both eyes → TIA / retinal artery occlusion → A&E same day
Palpitations with dizziness, presyncope, or fainting → arrhythmia → A&E
Progressive breathlessness at rest or lying flat → heart failure → urgent same-day review
diabetes: Hypoglycaemia (shaking, sweating, confusion): 15g fast carbohydrate, recheck in 15 min; if unconscious → A&E; call 1990
Vomiting + fruity breath + confusion + extreme thirst → DKA → A&E immediately
Non-healing foot wound, redness, or swelling → diabetic foot infection → same-day urgent review
Sudden vision change or new floaters → diabetic retinal haemorrhage → ophthalmology same day
renal: Sudden greatly reduced or absent urine output → AKI → A&E immediately; call 1990
Progressive bilateral leg or facial swelling + breathlessness → fluid retention → urgent review
Confusion or drowsiness in known CKD → uraemic encephalopathy → A&E
Muscle twitching or cramps in CKD → hyperkalaemia → urgent ECG
thyroid: Extreme cold intolerance + drowsiness + very low temperature → myxoedema coma → A&E
Rapid irregular heartbeat + fever + extreme agitation → thyroid storm → A&E immediately
New or rapidly enlarging neck lump → urgent ENT/endocrinology (within 2 weeks)
liver: Yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice) → urgent review within 24–48 hours
Vomiting blood or black tarry stools → upper GI bleed → A&E; call 1990
Severe right abdominal pain + fever → cholangitis / liver abscess → A&E
Confusion or drowsiness in known liver disease → hepatic encephalopathy → A&E
anaemia: Chest pain + breathlessness + palpitations in severe anaemia → cardiac decompensation → A&E
Active bleeding: heavy periods, black stools, blood in urine, haemoptysis → A&E if acute
universal: Unexplained weight loss >5 kg over 3 months → urgent malignancy screen
New persistent lump not resolving within 2–3 weeks → 2-week GP review
Night sweats + fever + lymph node swelling → haematological investigation
Persistent fatigue not improving with treatment → investigate for new pathology

annual_review_checklist: HbA1c (if diabetic, pre-diabetic, or on statin)
eGFR + U&E (if on ACEi/ARB, NSAID, or known CKD)
LFTs + CK if symptomatic (if on statin)
TSH (if on levothyroxine or known hypothyroid)
Exercise tolerance and physical activity assessment
